object_description: seven pavilion-like volumes arranged around generous interior courtyards
design_condition: The buildings are freely arranged along the site's northern perimeter as a counterpart to the southern buildings, preserving the central landmark while generating courtyards, walks, and sports spaces within the enclosure.

positive.statement: The pavilion style is skillfully adapted to the context, and the fragmented implementation preserves the monumental character of the central building.
The spatial organization fragments the built volume into medium-sized forms that evoke collective housing and a form of urbanity.
The arrangement offers great flexibility for future development and numerous phasing options.
The six divisions can house prisoners over time and establish a form of progression toward release.
The treatment of the facades integrates privacy requirements in relation to neighbours and walking spaces.
The stepped aggregation generates sub-spaces for sports and walks.
The delivery strategy is handled with great mastery and efficiency.

negative.statement: The longitudinal connection remains unclear, and its qualities of use are questionable in its current form.
Sections of the facade remain entirely blind.
The wall enclosure partly destroys the potential continuity of the landscape toward the distance.
The courtyard landscape variations are potentially interesting but remain embryonic and require particular attention.
